title: streaming-trajectory-checkpoints-heuristic-reconnect
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: Some customers using long-lived server-sent event (SSE) streams observe partial output duplication or gaps after transient network interruptions. Existing resume tokens are brittle for multi-part structured outputs (function calls + tool outputs) and older clients lack compatibility.

Goal: Implement a lightweight checkpointing approach — "trajectory checkpoints" — embedded in SSE chunks to allow heuristic reconnect and reassembly across mixed client versions. Ensure correct reconstruction for structured outputs (function/tool calls plus JSON records) and maintain backward compatibility with clients that do not negotiate checkpointing.

This ticket covers design, runtime changes to chunk framing, client negotiation headers, and a best-effort heuristic for reconnecting clients that missed checkpoints. It also captures fallbacks to existing resume token behavior and integration points with function-calling boundaries so that partially emitted tool-call payloads are not re-executed on reconnect.
acceptance_criteria: Protocol: SSE chunks may optionally include an s-checkpoint header with a monotonically increasing checkpoint id and byte-offset metadata
Backward compatibility: Clients that don't send 'X-RW-Checkpoint: 1' continue to get current resume-token behaviour unchanged
Reassembly: Server and client can rehydrate structured outputs (chat messages containing function_call blocks and tool result records) deterministically from checkpoint-aligned segments

Reconnect heuristic: On reconnect with last-checkpoint-id, server will provide the minimal re-stream window to allow client to reconcile duplicate partial messages without re-running tool side-effects
Tests: Integration tests covering duplicate suppression, gap healing, and mixed-version client interoperability pass in CI
Docs: API docs and migration guide updated with examples for SDKs (Node, Python) showing checkpoint negotiation and client-side reconciliation

technical_notes:
Approach summary:
1) Negotiation: Client may set header 'X-RW-Checkpoint: 1' when opening SSE. If present, server will emit an initial 'checkpoint:0' and subsequent 'checkpoint:<id>' lines as SSE comments (': checkpoint:42') plus structured metadata in a dedicated chunk type 'checkpoint-meta' for clients that parse full SSE fields.
2) Framing: Each logical token stream chunk will include 'chunk-id', 'checkpoint-id' and 'offset-in-checkpoint' fields. Checkpoint ids increase at function-call boundaries or after N bytes of JSON output (configurable).
3) Reconnect: On reconnect client sends 'Last-Checkpoint: <id>, Last-Offset: <offset>' as part of the Resume request. Server computes minimal window: if last checkpoint matches current head, server will stream from offset; if server no longer has data for that checkpoint, server falls back to resume-token semantics or full retransmit.
4) Heuristic dedupe: Server will include a short-lived dedupe token for each function_call invocation emitted in a checkpoint. The runtime will consult an idempotency cache to avoid re-running tool calls if the client requests replay that would otherwise re-trigger side-effects.

Tradeoffs and notes:
- Adds ~5-10% metadata overhead per chunk; mitigated by emitting checkpoints at coarse boundaries and compressing checkpoint-meta blobs.
- Complexity: requires changes across runtime, SDKs, and observability; doing incremental rollout under a feature flag reduces risk.
- Strong eventual correctness relies on runtime retaining checkpoint windows for at least 'checkpoint_retention_secs' (configurable). If retention lapses, we must gracefully fallback to previous resume-token behavior.

Implementation milestones:
- PoC server-side emission in dev environment (week 1)
- SDK sync + parsing helpers (week 2)
- Integration tests and idempotency cache (week 3)
- Gradual rollout and metrics (week 4)
